data.title: Nasdaq Futures Jump 2.5% as China Chip Stocks Soar Before Black Friday’s Early Close
data.description:
U.S. trading resumes on Black Friday, November 27, with Nasdaq-100 futures up 2.50% in the video’s 4:58 a.m. ET snapshot after a powerful rally in Chinese chip stocks. The rebound faces a shortened session and a market still nursing steep November losses. In today’s premarket video briefing, we look at the global chip rally, rising oil prices and Altria’s possible offer for Imperial Brands.

Wednesday’s regular session left a mixed starting point: the Dow erased a drop of more than 1,100 points to finish up 164.25 at 50,182.95, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.25% to 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% to 23,585.80. Through Wednesday, the S&P was up 3.94% for the week, the Nasdaq 4.28% and the Dow 4.23%. November remained negative: down 5.24%, 7.28% and 3.07%, respectively. Yesterday’s Thanksgiving briefing covers the session’s reversal and the economic releases.

President Trump challenged the upward revision to third-quarter GDP growth, to a 4.3% annual rate from 3.4%, calling it a “RECORD SETTING ERROR” that “should be immediately investigated.” CNBC reported Thursday that the revision was the largest since the second quarter of 2020, rather than a record, and that CME FedWatch showed traders pricing a nearly 100% chance of a December rate increase.

China supplied Friday’s strongest overseas move. A State Council meeting chaired by Premier Li Qiang called for a bigger market-support role for state-backed “national team” investors. The Shanghai Composite and CSI 300 recorded their largest daily gains since October 2024, Reuters reported. The video’s closing-data snapshot showed the STAR 50 up 15.07% at 1,346.25; the CSI Semiconductor index gained a record 17.4%, according to LSEG data cited by CNBC. South Korea’s Kospi rose 4.34% to 4,915.68 and the Kosdaq 8.13%; Japan’s Nikkei gained 2.11% to 58,711.11, while Taiwan’s Taiex added 0.40%. At 4:44 a.m. ET, Europe’s Stoxx 600 was about 1% higher and heading for its best week since May. Our earlier tariff report provides background on the trade-policy uncertainty.

At 4:58 a.m. ET Friday, the video’s Yahoo Finance futures snapshot put S&P 500 futures up 1.80%, Nasdaq-100 futures up 2.50% and Dow futures up 1.27%. Nasdaq premarket readings showed Micron (NASDAQ: MU) up 6.05%, AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) 6.30%, Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) 4.98%, Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) 4.68% and Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) 5.73%. Nvidia had lost 27% in November through Wednesday; our CreditWatch report explains its separate governance-related credit review. CNBC’s 4:59 a.m. ET Treasury reading put the 10-year yield at 4.91%, up 6.4 basis points from Wednesday. These are timestamped video-production readings, not refreshed quotes; CNBC’s live coverage tracks the session.

January WTI crude was $85.87 a barrel, up 2.62% from Wednesday’s settlement in the video’s 4:58 a.m. ET Friday snapshot, as tensions with Iran mounted. Kuwait said two Italians were killed by debris from Iranian attacks; Iran denied involvement. Israel said it was ready to strike Iran “at any moment,” even without U.S. forces, while Trump said the U.S. had “victory at hand,” CNBC reported.

Altria (NYSE: MO) confirmed Thursday that it is considering a possible offer for Imperial Brands, likely solely in cash, and is discussing a third party’s possible purchase of part of Imperial’s business. No agreement has been reached, and Imperial says it has received no approach. Altria faces a December 24 deadline for a firm offer or withdrawal, subject to an extension by the Takeover Panel. Imperial closed 13.3% higher in London Thursday at 3,432p, its highest since 2017; Altria was down 0.85% in the video’s premarket snapshot, measured at 4:55 a.m. ET. A possible bid remains distinct from an agreed takeover.

Stocks close at 1 p.m. ET today, and bonds at 2 p.m. Adobe forecasts Black Friday online sales of $12.9 billion, up 9.2%, and Cyber Monday sales of $15.1 billion. Those are forecasts; its reported November 1–22 spending was $82.5 billion, up 9.1%, as detailed in our holiday-spending report. Next week brings Jensen Huang’s closed-door House Foreign Affairs Committee appearance December 1 and Senate Banking Committee appearance December 3. The November jobs report arrives December 4 at 8:30 a.m. ET, ahead of the Fed’s December 8–9 meeting.

data.title: EU Leaders Nominate Pablo Hernández de Cos to Lead the ECB
data.description:
European Union leaders put forward Pablo Hernández de Cos on November 26 to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank. The former Bank of Spain governor would take over when Lagarde leaves on February 7, 2027, if the European Council confirms him after consulting the European Parliament and the ECB’s Governing Council.

Hernández de Cos has led the Bank for International Settlements since July 2025. He previously sat on the ECB’s rate-setting council while serving as Spain’s central bank governor from 2018 to 2024, according to the BIS. The European Council said the presidency carries a single eight-year term.

The nominations could change half of the ECB’s six-member executive board in the first half of 2027. EU leaders put forward Laurence Boone for the seat held by Isabel Schnabel, who plans to step down on January 3, and Markus Brunnermeier for Philip Lane’s seat when his term ends May 31. The Associated Press reported that Brunnermeier is a Princeton economist and Boone leads Santander’s corporate and investment banking business in France.

The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.50% in October. In an account of that meeting released November 26, the bank said many policymakers could have backed an increase as higher energy costs threatened to keep inflation elevated. Eurostat reported that annual euro-area inflation reached 4.0% in October, with energy accounting for nearly half of the increase in consumer prices over the year. Lagarde remains in charge for the December 16–17 rate meeting.

data.title: Tokyo Core Inflation Rises to 2.9% Ahead of Bank of Japan Meeting
data.description:
Core consumer prices in Tokyo rose 2.9% from a year earlier in November, up from 2.6% in October, Japan’s Statistics Bureau reported on November 27. It was the fastest increase since July 2025, Reuters reported, and gives the Bank of Japan another reason to consider raising rates in December.

The preliminary figures cover Tokyo’s 23 wards and come out ahead of the nationwide report. Japan’s core measure excludes fresh food and includes energy. Headline inflation edged up to 2.8% from 2.7%, while the index excluding both fresh food and energy slowed to 2.5% from 2.6%. The difference matters for policymakers weighing how broadly price pressures are spreading.

In a speech in Yamanashi a day before the release, Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura said the central bank should respond more quickly if shocks threaten to push underlying inflation above target. He argued that inflation expectations in Japan were still less firmly anchored, making a sustained rise in prices harder to reverse. His remarks reflected his own assessment as a board member.

The Bank of Japan’s current guideline is to keep its benchmark overnight rate around 1.25%. The board meets on December 17 and 18. The nationwide inflation report will give policymakers a broader view of whether Tokyo’s acceleration is showing up elsewhere in Japan.

data.title: Bank of Korea Raises Rate to 3.25% and Lifts Growth Outlook
data.description:
The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point to 3.25% on November 26. The central bank also raised its growth forecasts for this year and next, pointing to strong exports and investment driven by the semiconductor industry. Five policymakers backed the increase and two voted to hold the rate at 3%.

The bank now expects South Korea’s economy to grow 3.9% in 2026 and 4.1% in 2027, up from its August projections of 3.3% and 2.9%, respectively. It expects chip makers to continue supporting exports and investment, though it flagged uncertainty about how much of that strength will reach the rest of the economy.

Consumer prices and core prices, which exclude food and energy, both rose 2.8% from a year earlier in October, above the bank’s 2% inflation target. The bank cited persistent cost pressure and stronger demand as reasons inflation could stay above target. It raised its 2027 headline inflation forecast to 2.4% from 2.3% and flagged risks from household debt and the housing market around Seoul.

The decision followed a pause in October and marked the bank’s third increase this year, Reuters reported. The board said the timing of any further increase would depend on inflation, economic activity and financial stability.

data.title: U.S. Online Holiday Spending Rose 9.1% Before Thanksgiving, Adobe Finds
data.description:
U.S. shoppers spent $82.5 billion online from November 1 through 22, up 9.1% from the same stretch last year, according to Adobe Analytics figures reported by the Associated Press. The numbers give retailers an early measure of demand before the five-day stretch from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday.

Online spending passed $3 billion on each of the 22 days, according to Digital Commerce 360’s coverage of the Adobe data. Two days reached at least $4 billion, a first ahead of Thanksgiving in Adobe’s tracking. Purchases using buy now, pay later rose 6.5% to $6.1 billion over the same period. The figures measure spending in dollars, so they can move with prices as well as with how much people buy.

The early spending figures are separate from the forecasts for the holiday weekend. As noted in the Digest’s Thanksgiving briefing, Adobe expects $12.9 billion in online sales on Black Friday, up 9.2% year over year. It projects Cyber Monday will be the season’s biggest online shopping day at $15.1 billion, up 6.2%.

A separate National Retail Federation survey found that 183 million people expect to shop online or in stores between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday, including 126 million who plan to shop on Black Friday. The survey captures shoppers’ plans across both channels. Adobe’s early tally tracks online purchases already made.

data.title: Thanksgiving Market Briefing: Dow Erases 1,100-Point Drop as Inflation Hits 3.8%
data.description:
U.S. stock and bond markets are closed for Thanksgiving on Thursday, November 26, after the Dow erased a loss of more than 1,100 points Wednesday. Inflation and proposed tariffs remain in focus despite the comeback. In today’s holiday-edition video briefing, we trace Wednesday’s reversal, the inflation figures and the global rebound while U.S. cash markets take a break.

The Dow finished Wednesday’s regular session up 164.25 points, or 0.33%, at 50,182.95. The S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78 after losing as much as 3.2%; the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.62% to 23,585.80 after a 4.6% intraday drop. CNBC reported that traders attributed part of the recovery to thin holiday trading and a Michael Burry blog post saying he was “temporarily almost entirely long.” That was a sharp change from the weakness described in yesterday’s premarket briefing.

October’s PCE price index rose 3.8% from a year earlier, matching forecasts and accelerating from September’s 3.7%. Core inflation was 3.3%, above the 3.2% forecast. The BEA revised third-quarter GDP growth to a 4.3% annualized rate from 3.4%. Initial jobless claims were 189,000 against expectations of 200,000. CNBC said Wednesday markets fully priced a quarter-point rate increase at the December 8–9 Fed meeting. Our separate Beige Book report covers the Fed’s latest business survey.

The U.S. has proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners, with rates ranging from 15% to 35% and lower caps for countries with trade deals. China would face 20% on top of existing duties of roughly 25%. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said implementation was likely months away; China’s commerce ministry urged Washington to “rectify its wrongdoing,” CNBC reported Thursday. These are proposals, not tariffs already in force. The rates move the story beyond the anticipated announcement in our earlier investigation report.

Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) fell 3.91% to $149.30 Wednesday, leaving it down 27% in November. S&P Global placed its AA rating on CreditWatch Negative over governance concerns, as detailed in our credit-rating report. Micron (NASDAQ: MU) lost 4.53%, Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) 5.13% and Ambarella (NASDAQ: AMBA) 19.77% following a weak fourth-quarter outlook. HP (NYSE: HPQ) jumped 11.49% after beating expectations. Deere (NYSE: DE), Dell (NYSE: DELL) and Workday (NASDAQ: WDAY) reversed early losses to close up 4.44%, 0.60% and 0.68%, respectively. CNBC’s movers coverage describes the earnings reactions.

Thursday’s rebound extended abroad. At the Asian close, Taiwan’s Taiex rose 2.50%, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng 1.19%, Japan’s Nikkei 225 0.86% and South Korea’s Kospi 0.29%. Europe was higher, with Germany’s DAX up 1.95% at 10:17 a.m. CET, or 4:17 a.m. ET, in the video’s CNBC quote snapshot. CNBC’s global-market report tracks the overseas recovery.

At 4:31 a.m. ET Thursday, the video’s Yahoo Finance futures snapshot showed S&P 500 futures up 0.39%, Nasdaq-100 futures up 0.38% and Dow futures up 0.30%. These are the video’s timestamped readings, not refreshed quotes. Futures trading is distinct from the closed U.S. cash market; there is no U.S. stock premarket session today.

Stocks reopen Friday, November 27, with a 1 p.m. ET early close; bonds close at 2 p.m. ET. For Black Friday, Adobe forecasts $12.9 billion in online sales, up 9.2%. Next week brings Jensen Huang’s appearances before the House Foreign Affairs Committee on December 1 and Senate Banking Committee on December 3, followed by the November jobs report on December 4 at 8:30 a.m. ET.

data.title: Fed Beige Book Finds Business Costs Rising Faster Than Selling Prices
data.description:
Businesses across the United States reported that their costs generally rose faster than the prices they charged customers, according to the Federal Reserve’s November Beige Book. The report, released November 25, said firms faced higher expenses for items such as freight, insurance and imported materials. Competition and price-sensitive shoppers limited how much businesses could pass on.

Economic activity expanded slightly to moderately in eight of the 12 Fed districts and was unchanged in the other four. Consumer spending changed little overall as households grew more selective about discretionary purchases. Auto sales softened, and housing activity weakened as high borrowing costs made purchases harder to afford.

Manufacturing grew modestly, with some suppliers seeing stronger demand even as producers tied to housing and consumer goods struggled. The Cleveland Fed reported that data center projects, power generation and defense supported manufacturing demand in its district. Contacts there said data center demand lengthened delivery times for chips and electrical components.

Employment edged up overall. Many companies kept head counts steady and hired mostly to replace departing workers. Wages and benefits grew moderately, picking up from the previous report.

The Atlanta Fed compiled the survey using information collected through November 16. The report gives policymakers a view of how businesses are managing higher costs ahead of the December 8–9 Fed meeting.

data.title: S&P Puts Nvidia’s AA Credit Rating on Downgrade Watch
data.description:
S&P Global Ratings placed the AA credit rating of Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) on CreditWatch Negative on November 25. The rating remains AA while S&P reviews whether to lower it. The agency cited concerns about how the chipmaker’s directors oversee management after Jensen Huang’s departure and return as chief executive.

S&P said the leadership change left questions about how Nvidia’s board enforces its rules for executives, Reuters reported. The rating agency plans to meet with directors and management to discuss board independence, oversight of executives and succession planning, according to Investing.com.

Nvidia announced Huang’s return on Monday. In its filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the company said his reinstatement followed consultation with senior U.S. officials. It said an independent board committee would continue its investigation and that Nvidia had started a search for a chief compliance officer.

The review puts those governance questions in front of Nvidia’s bondholders. A lower rating can affect the interest rate investors demand on new debt, and S&P said it could act within 90 days. The agency expects any cut to be one notch unless new information points to damage to Nvidia’s reputation or business, Reuters reported.

data.title: Tech Sell-Off Deepens Before Thanksgiving; Dell Slides Despite Earnings Beat
data.description:
U.S. stock futures fell sharply before the open on Wednesday, November 25, as the retreat in AI shares spread through Asian markets. Strong Dell results failed to lift its stock, while reports of new U.S. tariffs added another uncertainty ahead of a packed economic calendar and the Thanksgiving holiday.

Premarket update: At 7:06 a.m. ET, delayed CNBC futures quotes showed December Nasdaq-100 futures down 3.01% at 25,484.50, S&P 500 futures down 2.00% at 7,073.50 and Dow futures down 1.32% at 49,398. In today’s pre-market video briefing, we look at the AI reversal, Dell’s earnings and the data due before Thanksgiving. These refreshed readings differ from the video’s 6:19 a.m. ET snapshot, when Nasdaq-100 futures were down about 2.4%.

Tuesday’s regular session had already split Wall Street. The S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 1.48% to 23,733.54, while the Dow gained 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70, back above 50,000, according to CNBC’s closing report. That reversed part of the tech rally described in yesterday’s briefing. The Conference Board consumer confidence index rose to 103.3, well above the 92.2 Dow Jones consensus.

Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) fell 5.86% Tuesday to $155.38, a day after gaining roughly 31%. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) dropped 11%, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) lost 8.9% and Analog Devices (NASDAQ: ADI) slid 17% despite beating quarterly expectations. Anthropic fell 6.5% to $81.91, below its $83 IPO price. Retailers moved the other way: Abercrombie & Fitch (NYSE: ANF) rose 19.7%, Dick’s Sporting Goods (NYSE: DKS) gained 14.6% and Kohl’s (NYSE: KSS) added 19.5%. CNBC’s movers coverage detailed the earnings behind those divergent reactions; our Analog Devices report covers its results.

Following Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO, he told employees that the company had built a team that did not require succession planning, CNBC reported, citing people in the room. President Donald Trump told the New York Post a pardon was “always an option” but probably would not be “necessary,” according to CNBC. Huang faces a closed-door House Foreign Affairs interview on December 1 and a Senate Banking hearing on December 3.

Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103%, and adjusted EPS of $9.45 against the $6.59 LSEG estimate. AI server revenue rose 291% to $22.0 billion, with a $132.3 billion AI backlog. Dell raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $202 billion and added $25 billion to its buyback authorization. Its fourth-quarter forecast of $8.40 in adjusted EPS and about $56.3 billion in revenue also beat LSEG estimates of $7.50 and $53.61 billion. Yet Dell fell another 6.37% to $276.48 at 7:16 a.m. ET in CNBC premarket quotes, after Tuesday’s 11.8% regular-session decline. Our Dell earnings report has the broader breakdown.

At 7:16 a.m. ET, CNBC quotes put Nvidia down 5.20% at $147.30 and Anthropic down 4.14% at $78.52. Other earnings reactions were also negative: Workday (NASDAQ: WDAY) was down 7.38% at $166.00 at 7:14 a.m.; Ambarella (NASDAQ: AMBA) fell 33.66% to $29.50 at 7:15 a.m.; and Deere (NYSE: DE) lost 2.57% to $598.00 at 7:13 a.m. ET. These premarket readings also differ from the video’s earlier snapshot.

Workday beat quarterly earnings and revenue expectations, but free cash flow of $691 million missed the $712 million LSEG estimate. Its fourth-quarter subscription revenue forecast is $2.600 billion, up 10%; our Workday report covers the annual outlook. Ambarella guided fourth-quarter revenue to $70–75 million against a $112 million LSEG estimate, according to CNBC. Deere reported fourth-quarter EPS of $3.89, down from $3.93 a year earlier, and forecast fiscal 2027 net income of $4.50–5.25 billion.

In Wednesday’s Asian session, South Korea’s Kospi fell 6.16% to 4,697.51, back below 5,000. Taiwan’s Taiex lost 4.80% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 2.78%, according to CNBC’s market coverage. That report also highlighted possible new tariffs covering more than a dozen trading partners, including China and the European Union. Our tariff report explains the investigation; proposed duties and reports of plans should not be treated as tariffs already in force.

At 8:30 a.m. ET, the BEA is scheduled to release October personal income and spending, including PCE inflation, and the second estimate of third-quarter GDP. Dow Jones consensus calls for headline PCE prices to rise 0.3% month over month and 3.8% year over year, according to CNBC. Durable goods orders and weekly jobless claims are also due at 8:30 a.m. ET. U.S. stock markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and at 1 p.m. ET Friday; the bond market’s Friday close is 2 p.m. ET, according to CNBC’s holiday schedule.

data.title: What’s Ahead for the Stock Market This Week
data.description:
After Friday’s sharp selloff triggered by President Trump’s decision to raise tariffs in response to China tightening rare earth exports, investors are starting the week on edge. The focus now shifts to trade tensions, earnings season, and the Federal Reserve’s next moves.

Big Earnings Week: Banks and Chipmakers Take Center Stage

This week kicks off a busy stretch of third-quarter results from major financial firms and tech companies.

  • Banks: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Citigroup all report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Later in the week, American Express, Truist Financial, and State Street will wrap up the financial lineup.
  • Tech & Chips: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) reports Thursday after strong AI chip sales boosted its revenue 40% in the first half of 2025. ASML follows on Wednesday after raising concerns about tariffs and slowing demand for chip equipment.
  • Tech events: Oracle’s AI World conference begins Monday, and Salesforce’s Dreamforce starts Tuesday — both likely to bring attention to artificial intelligence and enterprise tech. Earnings Calendar >>

Data Delays and Fed Watch

The federal government shutdown, now entering its third week, is likely to delay several key reports, including retail sales, inflation (PPI), housing starts, and jobless claims. Some data will still come through, like the NFIB Small Business Optimism Index on Tuesday and homebuilder confidence on Thursday.

Investors will also tune in to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s speech on Tuesday, along with comments from Fed officials, including Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller. The Fed’s Beige Book, which gives an overview of economic conditions across regions, will be released on Wednesday.

Market Context

Bond markets will be closed on Monday for Columbus Day (also observed as Indigenous Peoples Day), but stock exchanges will remain open.

With limited economic data and uncertainty around Washington’s budget standoff, markets are likely to take their cues from corporate earnings and Fed commentary.

In short, this week is about navigating through noise — balancing worries over tariffs and the shutdown against potential optimism from strong bank and chipmaker earnings.
